title: Frankie Dusen's band and Joe Howard
summary: He recalls Frankie Dusen's band with trumpeter Joe Howard, who later played tuba, and where Dusen lived and what he played.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who was in his band?

Huh? Who was in his band? Uh, let me see, uh, the trumpet player was, uh, I know you know him, uh, what do you call this man? I don't know much about Franky Dusen. I don't know much about Franky Dusen. There he is. He never had my tongue, I think.
Where did he live?
Where did he live? He used to live from Franklin, between, uh, uh, uh, uh, uh, Taladona, but he moved out on Janet Taylor between Collison and Cessna. That's where he died up there.
He said, uh, I can't figure out who that is.

Joe Howard. Joe Howard? Joe Howard, yeah. You remember Joe Howard, yeah. Oh, yeah. Uh, then he stopped, he stopped playing, and went to play bass, tuba, yeah. Mm-hmm. I played with him a good while, too. Uh, and, uh, he said, yeah, he got too old for his trumpet, so he got on, uh, bass, tuba, you know. And he used to teach, too. He was a good musician. Yes, indeed. And, uh, this son, this son Johnson, you know him?
Uh, that's the son. Yeah.

I've never heard him. Never heard him. Oh, he was good. He teaches school, him and Rudy Humphrey, over that night. Yeah, he was good. He had been to office, but he didn't, he didn't take him. He stayed up there. And after he got married, I believe he got about eight or nine kids on there.
Who did he work with?

What do you think? Who did he work with? We used to work with all these bands down there. All the big shot bands. He, he worked with me and Kid Hire as well. And we was the first one to hire them. Had them with the band. Then after he got good, well, uh, Sidney Desiree got in. And then, uh, after Sidney, they got on the boat to speak Marvin. And different bands he used to play with.
